---
title: GitHub Repositories
---

The **GitHub repositories** workflow incrementally maintains a complete Git
mirror and optionally collects Git LFS objects, the wiki, repository metadata,
and release assets. It then snapshots the managed workspace to one or more
configured restic repositories.

## Configure a job

GitHub jobs live in `backups`, but use `github` instead of `paths`:

```yaml
backups:
  - job-id: example-github-repository
    description: Complete GitHub repository backup.
    restic-repository-ids:
      - personal-b2
      - personal-local
    tag: example-github-repository
    github:
      repository-url: git@github.com:example/example-repository.git
      authentication:
        git:
          ssh:
            private-key:
              file: /var/run/secrets/github/ssh-private-key
            known-hosts:
              file: /var/run/secrets/github/known-hosts
        api:
          token:
            env: GITHUB_MIGRATION_TOKEN
      components:
        git: true
        lfs: true
        wiki: true
        metadata: true
        release-assets: true
      migration-timeout-seconds: 3600
```

Every component flag is required, and at least one must be `true`. `lfs`
requires `git`. A GitHub job cannot also define `paths`. The optional restic
`tag` still defaults to `job-id`.

Only `github.com` clone URLs are accepted:

```text
git@github.com:OWNER/REPOSITORY.git
https://github.com/OWNER/REPOSITORY.git
```

Credentials, query strings, and fragments embedded in the URL are rejected.

## Credentials

Every configured secret source contains exactly one `env` or `file` key. The
environment variable or file is read again on every run, which works with
rotated Kubernetes Secrets and other secret managers. Secret values are never
placed in command arguments, logs, manifests, or the audit log.

For SSH clone URLs, omit `authentication.git` to use the existing SSH agent and
configuration, or configure both a private key and `known_hosts`. Configured
keys are copied to temporary owner-only files, and strict host verification is
always enabled. Generate a pinned host entry according to GitHub's
[SSH host key guidance](https://docs.github.com/en/authentication/keeping-your-account-and-data-secure/githubs-ssh-key-fingerprints).

For HTTPS clone URLs, use a token without putting it in the URL:

```yaml
authentication:
  git:
    https:
      token:
        env: GITHUB_GIT_TOKEN
```

The CLI supplies it through a temporary Git askpass helper. Public HTTPS
repositories may omit Git authentication.

The separate `authentication.api.token` is required when `metadata` or
`release-assets` is enabled. GitHub's migration API currently requires a
compatible **classic personal access token** and repository-owner access;
fine-grained tokens and GitHub App tokens are not supported for this API. See
GitHub's [organization migration API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/migrations/orgs)
and [user migration API](https://docs.github.com/en/rest/migrations/users).

For a Kubernetes CronJob, mount files or inject environment variables from a
Secret and point the job at their names—do not put secret values in YAML:

```yaml
env:
  - name: GITHUB_MIGRATION_TOKEN
    valueFrom:
      secretKeyRef:
        name: github-backup
        key: api-token
volumeMounts:
  - name: github-ssh
    mountPath: /var/run/secrets/github
    readOnly: true
```

The container needs `git`, `git-lfs` when LFS is enabled, `gh` when API-backed
components are enabled, and `restic`. `make install-deps` installs these tools
with Homebrew for local use.

## Components

| Component | Backed-up data | Update behavior |
|---|---|---|
| `git` | Every Git ref and object, including full branch and tag history | Initial `git clone --mirror`; later `git remote update --prune` |
| `lfs` | All Git LFS objects reachable from the mirror | `git lfs fetch --all origin` |
| `wiki` | The repository wiki as a separate Git mirror | Missing or empty wikis are recorded as `not-present` |
| `metadata` | GitHub's official migration export, including issues, pull requests, comments, attachments, and release metadata | A new migration archive is requested and downloaded each run |
| `release-assets` | Binary files attached to releases | Missing or changed assets download atomically; remotely deleted assets are removed only after a complete successful update |

A Git-only job sets `git: true` and every other component to `false`. It needs
only Git authentication and never invokes `gh`. Git history contains commits,
branches, and tags; it does **not** contain issue discussions, pull-request
comments, or other GitHub database records. Without `lfs`, Git history still
contains LFS pointer files but not the referenced large objects.

## Run and inspect

Use the described arrow-key TUI or explicit commands:

```sh
uv run restic-backups github-repository list
uv run restic-backups github-repository backup example-github-repository \
  --repository personal-b2 --repository personal-local
uv run restic-backups github-repository status
uv run restic-backups github-repository status example-github-repository
uv run restic-backups github-repository data-dir example-github-repository
```

With no job ID, `status` shows one row for every GitHub job and destination,
including the latest snapshot ID and time, the local export time, and component
states. Snapshots are matched using each job's configured tag, which defaults to
its job ID. Each destination repository is queried only once, even when many
jobs share it. Passing a job ID limits the snapshot table and adds that job's
detailed component errors.

The status table reads restic snapshot metadata, not backed-up file contents.
It can contact remote storage when the required metadata is not already cached.

The TUI starts with every configured destination unchecked. Select each desired
restic repository with Space. A dry run validates the plan without calling Git,
GitHub, or restic and without writing the workspace:

```sh
uv run restic-backups github-repository backup example-github-repository \
  --repository personal-b2 --dry-run
```

## Managed workspace and snapshots

The reusable local workspace lives beside the selected config:

```text
data/github-repositories/<job-id>/
  repository.git/
  wiki.git/
  github-export/
  release-assets/
  backup-manifest.json
```

The manifest records the source, update time, and a safe status for every
component: `updated`, `unchanged`, `stale`, `not-present`, `failed`, or
`disabled`. If one component fails, the workflow still attempts the others and
all selected destinations. Existing local component data is included as
`stale`; the command creates the best available snapshot and exits nonzero when
anything failed. Disabled cached components are not included.

Restic splits input into content-defined chunks and deduplicates identical
chunks **within each restic repository**. Stable Git pack files, LFS objects,
migration files, and release assets therefore do not need to be uploaded again.
The workflow disables automatic Git maintenance and repacking because repacking
can rewrite otherwise unchanged Git objects and reduce deduplication. Separate
restic repositories do not share chunks, so two destinations each store their
own copy. See restic's [repository design](https://restic.readthedocs.io/en/stable/100_references.html#repository-design).

Restore a snapshot with the normal restic command, then clone the restored bare
repository into a working tree:

```sh
uv run restic-backups generic restic run --backup example-github-repository \
  restore latest --target /tmp/github-restore
git clone /tmp/github-restore/repository.git restored-repository
```

## Deliberate limits

This workflow does not export GitHub Actions artifacts, logs or caches,
packages, secret values, forks as independent repositories, submodule
repositories, or GitHub Enterprise. Configure another job for each independent
Git or submodule repository that must be retained.
